title: Gmail and CRM, account A: six decisions
audience: Dinis: six decisions from the first day of account A's Gmail and CRM team
summary: The team built the send screen, a lead board and a synthetic demo on branches. Six decisions and one task wait on Dinis; each has a recommendation.

beats.narration: In its first half hour (go about 14:50 UTC, now 15:15), account A's Gmail and CRM team built a send screen, a lead board and a shared synthetic demo. Six things now wait on you. Here they are, each with a recommendation.

What exists, on branches, not live. The send screen follows your G3: pick a contact, see the draft, edit, press Send. The lead board shows every company's stage, draft and follow-ups. Both run on made-up data in demo mode.

One: release the send screen to the live site. 122 tests and every gate pass, and nothing overlaps account D's waiting release. It sends real mail only after you confirm, at most 20 a day. We recommend yes.

items: Real mode: your Gmail, your press, 20 a day
Gates OK; no overlap with release/next2

beats.narration: Two: where the send screen finds recipients for real. Typed by hand today. Your sent mail, read in your browser only, is quick. The lead board and outbox are the lasting answer. We recommend hand-typed now, the lead board later.

left.title: Your sent mail
points: Reads more of your mail in the page

right.title: Lead board and outbox
points: Needs the outbox key at outreach@ first

beats.narration: Three and four are housekeeping. The public demo vault's read key needs one narrow leak-scan allowance to be written down. And three abandoned vaults of made-up data can go: one had its passphrase printed, two hold old names. We recommend yes to both.

items: Demo read key: one allowlist line for it
Delete a5a7rrbl (passphrase printed in a session)
Delete epk5452e and db5vicpi (old names; a slip made the second)

beats.narration: Five: a.crm.dev asked to read four repositories, among them the team CRM and the AWS platform, so its records match ours. That prompt waits in its session. We recommend approving read-only access.

visual.label: repositories, read-only, waiting in a.crm.dev's session

beats.narration: Six: the documentation pages: how to use the tools, how to run your own copy with your own Google app, and how to join. They speak for the team, so they go live on your word. We recommend yes after your read.

items: Run your own, with your own Google OAuth app

beats.narration: And one task only you can do, from your G4 yes: ask Google to review the site in Search Console. Until then, every link from outreach or the hub lands on a red warning. The narration voice is synthetic.

visual.text: Your task: request the Safe Browsing review

decisions.question: D1. Release the send screen (work/mail.dev.a) to dev, which is the live site?

options.label: Yes
good: G3 live for you and the team
bad: A new real-send page on a site Google flags

decisions.why: Reviewed, tested, gated; sending stays your press and confirm.

decisions.question: D2. Where does the send screen find recipients in real mode?

options.label: Your sent mail, read in your browser only
bad: The page reads more of your mail

options.label: Hand-typed now; the lead board and outbox later
bad: Waits on the outbox key at outreach@

decisions.why: Keeps one list of who we write to, as G4 puts private mail on the Web Summit side.

decisions.question: D3. Where may the public demo vault's read key be written?

options.label: One narrow allowlist line in the leak scan for that key only
good: Docs and hub can link the demo

decisions.why: Your ask: demos everyone can see, on synthetic data.

decisions.question: D4. Delete the abandoned synthetic vaults a5a7rrbl, epk5452e and db5vicpi; leave the old made-up names in work/crm.dev.a's git history?

options.label: Delete the three vaults; leave the branch history
good: No stray vaults or printed passphrase
No force-push of a pushed branch
bad: Made-up names that may match real firms stay in old commits (never labelled as real)

options.label: Delete the three vaults and rewrite the branch history
good: Old names gone from the branch
bad: Force-push; GitHub still keeps the objects by id

options.label: Keep everything
bad: A vault whose passphrase was printed stays

decisions.why: Synthetic data only; a history rewrite costs more than it removes.

decisions.question: D5. a.crm.dev's read-only add-repo for four repositories (in its session)?

options.label: Approve
good: CRM records match the team CRM
bad: Wider read access for one session

options.label: Refuse
bad: CRM record names stay a guess

decisions.why: Read only; it cannot align with the team CRM otherwise.

decisions.question: D6. Publish the three documentation pages (after your read)?

options.label: Yes
bad: Not yet followed by an outsider

decisions.why: They are marked as drafts until an outsider has followed them.
